summary: A narrator, after leaving Lou at a hospital where he is sedated following a minor cut, goes home around 2:15 a.m. and books a 9:30 a.m. American Airlines flight. He has come to believe Alex Goddard's Children of Light and its Guatemalan accomplices are illegally obtaining white babies and may be involved in kidnapping, and Sarah has been taken. He feels intense guilt over having failed Sarah for years, and resolves to wake Steve to start making it up to her.
one_line: A narrator books a dawn flight after Lou is hospitalized and Sarah is taken, linking Alex Goddard's Children of Light to illegal baby trafficking.
key_facts: Lou is told by a doctor that his injury is a superficial cut and he should not be playing handball for a few days.
Visiting hours at the hospital have long passed, and the narrator may visit after two P.M. the next day.
The narrator tells Lou he can call 26 Federal Plaza in the morning to see what they can do.
After helping fill out insurance forms, the narrator takes a cab downtown to retrieve his Toyota.
The time is two-fifteen in the morning when the narrator gets home.
The narrator calls American Airlines and books a flight at nine-thirty in the morning.
The narrator now believes Alex Goddard's Children of Light and its Guatemalan accomplices are completely illegal rather than merely shady.
The narrator suspects the group is getting hundreds of white babies in ways that could not bear the light of day.
The narrator says the Army is involved and Sarah's abduction makes the group's game feel like kidnapping.
The narrator describes Sarah as a pawn, and says it is all because of him.
The narrator's guilt about Sarah has lasted for the past fifteen years.
The narrator did not fly back for Sarah's high school graduation because he was cramming for grad school finals.
The narrator resolves to wake Steve and start making it up to Sarah.
